summary: Backend-only testing of ZedPulse newly-added endpoints: emergency contact, food scanner (library/log/scans/scan), clinic finder (~40 clinics with city filter), and weekly insights. Built /app/backend/tests/test_08_zedpulse.py with 27 tests. 26/27 PASSED. 1 FAILED: POST /api/food/scan returns 502 for a valid JPEG — the backend wraps the image in FileContent(content_type='image/jpeg') but emergentintegrations/litellm's OpenAI route for gpt-5.6-terra sends it through the file-upload path which expects application/pdf, so the vision call never succeeds. Fix: use emergentintegrations.llm.chat.ImageContent instead of FileContent. All other endpoints (emergency contact GET/POST/DELETE with validation + upsert, food library 30 items, food log, food scan input validation, 40 clinics with Lusaka=18 and Ndola=3 subsets, weekly insights shape with and without seeded readings) behave exactly as specified. Auth enforcement verified: all new endpoints 401 without token except public /food/library and /clinics.

critical.issue: Vision call always fails with 502. Backend uses FileContent(content_type='image/jpeg', file_content_base64=...) at server.py:858; emergentintegrations/litellm routes this through OpenAI's files/PDF API and rejects image/jpeg: `Invalid file data: ... Expected a base64-encoded data URL with an application/pdf MIME type ... but got unsupported MIME type 'image/jpeg'`. Fix: `from emergentintegrations.llm.chat import ImageContent` and pass `file_contents=[ImageContent(image_base64=input.image_base64)]`. The whole Food Scanner feature is broken end-to-end until this is fixed.

minor.issue: Phone validation uses `len(normalize_phone(phone)) < 7` which only checks digit count. A string like '+2601234' (7 digits) is accepted even though it is not a valid Zambian MSISDN. If stricter Zambian validation is desired (expected +260 followed by 9 digits), add a regex check. Current behaviour matches the spec's '>=7' rule, so not a blocker.

`tip` is empty string when there are no readings (expected). When readings exist, the LLM call is best-effort — if it fails, `tip` is '' and the endpoint still returns 200. This matches the spec ('may be empty if no readings') but note that network/LLM errors are also silently swallowed to tip=''.

critical_code_review_comments: Food Scanner integration path uses the wrong emergentintegrations class — ImageContent is the dedicated subclass for vision input; FileContent is for PDF uploads. The library docstring makes this clear.

The 502 is actually a 500 from the backend being surfaced by the ingress; the backend logs raise HTTPException(502, ...) inside food_scan after catching the LLM exception. Users will see a confusing Cloudflare page instead of the JSON error.
`import json as _json, re as _re` inside the endpoint body (server.py:866) — move to module top for consistency.
ZAMBIAN_FOODS and ZAMBIAN_CLINICS are large module-level constants (~70 LOC each); move to a data/ json file or a separate module to shrink server.py.

`weekly_insights` embeds a 7-day LLM call on the hot path; if the model is slow this blocks the request. Consider caching the tip per (user_id, iso-week) in Mongo so repeat calls in the same week are instant.

rca_of_issue:
RCA for POST /api/food/scan 502:
  Trigger: Any client posts a valid base64 JPEG to /api/food/scan with Authorization bearer token.
  Server logs (backend.err.log):
    litellm.exceptions.BadRequestError: OpenAIException - Invalid file data: 'messages[2].content[0].file.file_data'. Expected a base64-encoded data URL with an application/pdf MIME type ... but got unsupported MIME type 'image/jpeg'. Received Model Group=gpt-5.6-terra
  Root cause: server.py imports `FileContent` and constructs `FileContent(content_type='image/jpeg', file_content_base64=input.image_base64)`. The emergentintegrations.llm.chat module serialises FileContent through OpenAI's `file` content-part (intended for PDFs), not through the vision `image_url` content-part. The library ships a dedicated subclass `ImageContent(image_base64=...)` which routes correctly to the vision API.
  Reproduction:
    1. POST /api/auth/signup to get a token.
    2. POST /api/food/scan with any base64 JPEG >100 bytes and Authorization header.
    3. Observe 502 (backend raises HTTPException(502) after catching ChatError).
  Mitigation / fix:
    1. Edit /app/backend/server.py near line 11 imports: `from emergentintegrations.llm.chat import LlmChat, UserMessage, ImageContent` (remove or keep FileContent as needed).
    2. In food_scan() (line ~856), replace `FileContent(content_type=..., file_content_base64=input.image_base64)` with `ImageContent(image_base64=input.image_base64)`.
    3. `sudo supervisorctl restart backend` then rerun the failing test — it should return 200 with the documented JSON contract (even for non-food images, foods=[] is acceptable per spec).
